## Evidence-backed failure mechanisms

These selected cases explain mechanisms, not benchmark prevalence. They do not render query text, candidate responses, private identifiers, raw artifacts, or model rationale.

<section class="hub-failure-record" data-failure-mechanism="fusion-dilution">
<h2>Fusion dilution</h2>
<dl class="hub-failure-fields">
<dt>What failed</dt>
<dd>21 development failures: One promoted component already ranks the official positive in its top ten, but equal reciprocal-rank fusion does not.</dd>
<dt>Evidence available</dt>
<dd>The canonical development-only diagnostic separates the two promoted component rankings from their equal reciprocal-rank fusion.</dd>
<dt>Response or change</dt>
<dd>Do not retune a static mixture post hoc; test a preregistered preservation gate or a bounded adaptive rule against the frozen control.</dd>
<dt>Observed outcome</dt>
<dd>A component's top-ten signal can be moved out of the fused top ten.</dd>
<dt>Possible failure location</dt>
<dd>The equal reciprocal-rank fusion step after component rankings are formed.</dd>
<dt>Competing explanation</dt>
<dd>The component signal may be incidental or insufficiently robust, rather than fusion alone being the cause.</dd>
<dt>Confirmed defect, audit gap, or uncertainty</dt>
<dd>Confirmed diagnostic mechanism in the selected development cohort; it is not a hidden-test defect finding.</dd>
<dt>Evidence limit</dt>
<dd>Post-hoc development audit with unavailable target responses and assessor rationale.</dd>
<dt>Next falsifying test</dt>
<dd><a href="../generated/ideas/failure-aware-fusion.qmd">Failure-aware evidence fusion</a> must beat the frozen dense/profile control under a fixed decision rule.</dd>
<dt>Source study and evidence status</dt>
<dd><a href="../studies/sparse-failure-analogue-diagnosis.qmd">Sparse-failure analogue diagnosis</a> — concluded development-only diagnostic.</dd>
</dl>
</section>

<section class="hub-failure-record" data-failure-mechanism="no-component-signal">
<h2>No component signal</h2>
<dl class="hub-failure-fields">
<dt>What failed</dt>
<dd>54 development failures: Neither promoted component ranks the official positive in its top ten.</dd>
<dt>Evidence available</dt>
<dd>The canonical development-only diagnostic shows neither promoted component supplied a top-ten signal.</dd>
<dt>Response or change</dt>
<dd>Do not reweight the same lists as a recovery; introduce a new, frozen evidence source or stop the proposed change.</dd>
<dt>Observed outcome</dt>
<dd>Fusion cannot recover a relevant candidate absent from both component top tens.</dd>
<dt>Possible failure location</dt>
<dd>Upstream retrieval or candidate-side evidence construction before fusion.</dd>
<dt>Competing explanation</dt>
<dd>Historical analogues may be too weak, or the available component representations may omit the needed expertise signal.</dd>
<dt>Confirmed defect, audit gap, or uncertainty</dt>
<dd>Confirmed missing component signal in the selected development cohort; the missing evidence source is still uncertain.</dd>
<dt>Evidence limit</dt>
<dd>Development-only post-hoc diagnosis does not reveal the target response or establish hidden-test frequency.</dd>
<dt>Next falsifying test</dt>
<dd><a href="../generated/ideas/semantic-failure-clusters.qmd">Semantic failure clusters</a> must identify a reproducible new signal beyond the frozen components.</dd>
<dt>Source study and evidence status</dt>
<dd><a href="../studies/sparse-failure-analogue-diagnosis.qmd">Sparse-failure analogue diagnosis</a> — concluded development-only diagnostic.</dd>
</dl>
</section>

<section class="hub-failure-record" data-failure-mechanism="unreliable-generated-evidence">
<h2>Unreliable generated evidence</h2>
<dl class="hub-failure-fields">
<dt>What failed</dt>
<dd>Generated reference evidence can be ambiguous, unsupported, or insufficiently grounded for an automatic ranking decision.</dd>
<dt>Evidence available</dt>
<dd>Selected grounding, corpus-quality, and blinded reference-review audits identify uncertainty, provenance, and disagreement risks.</dd>
<dt>Response or change</dt>
<dd>Use explicit uncertainty and review gates; develop a reproducible disagreement trigger instead of grounding every request.</dd>
<dt>Observed outcome</dt>
<dd>Grounding and review are useful safeguards, but not reliable blanket cures or validated ground truth.</dd>
<dt>Possible failure location</dt>
<dd>Reference generation, Search grounding, source support, or the trigger that decides when review is required.</dd>
<dt>Competing explanation</dt>
<dd>Reviewer noise or purposive sampling may explain part of the observed disagreement.</dd>
<dt>Confirmed defect, audit gap, or uncertainty</dt>
<dd>An audit gap and reliability uncertainty remain; no universal generated-evidence defect has been established.</dd>
<dt>Evidence limit</dt>
<dd>No prevalence count is available. The audits use selected or purposive samples and do not estimate a population rate.</dd>
<dt>Next falsifying test</dt>
<dd><a href="../generated/ideas/reference-review-trigger.qmd">Reference review trigger</a> must show that a frozen trigger improves reliability without treating all generated evidence as false.</dd>
<dt>Source study and evidence status</dt>
<dd><a href="../studies/gemini-grounding-failure-review.qmd">Gemini grounding failure review</a>, <a href="../studies/grounded-data-quality-audit.qmd">grounded reference data-quality audit</a>, and <a href="../studies/four-model-reference-review.qmd">four-model reference-answer review</a> — concluded selected-audit and purposive-review evidence.</dd>
</dl>
</section>
